name: Alcaeus of Lesbos
bio: Alcaeus of Lesbos is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 7th century BC. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of Meleager's Wreath, the Garland compiled about 100 BC.
This archive carries the 2 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the first volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Books I–VI) (Book V: 10; Book VI: 218).

poems.title: Book V, 10
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: The Greek Anthology (Loeb, vol. I, 1916)
poems.text: I hate Love. Why doth not his heavy godship attack wild beasts, but shooteth ever at my heart? What gain is it for a god to burn up a man, or what trophies of price shall he win from my head?

poems.title: Book VI, 218
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: The Greek Anthology (Loeb, vol. I, 1916)
poems.text: A begging eunuch priest of Cybele was wandering through the upland forests of Ida, and there met him a huge lion, its hungry throat dreadfully gaping as though to devour him. Then in fear of the death that faced him in its ravening jaws, he beat his tambour from the holy grove. The lion shut its murderous mouth, and as if itself full of divine frenzy, began to toss and whirl its mane about its neck. But he thus escaping a dreadful death dedicated to Rhea the beast that had taught itself her dance.

poems.title: Book VII, 55: On the Same
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: The Greek Anthology (Loeb, vol. II, 1917)
poems.note: Attribution doubtful in Paton (Alcaeus of Mytilene or of Messene).
poems.text: In a shady grove of Locris the Nymphs washed the body of Hesiod with water from their springs and raised a tomb to him. And on it the goat-herds poured libations of milk mixed with golden honey. For even such was the song the old man breathed who had tasted the pure fountains of the nine Muses.

poems.title: To Apollo (Fragment 1)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book I, Hymns
poems.text:
O King Apollo, son of great Zeus,
e.g. whom thy father did furnish forth at thy birth with golden headband and lyre of shell, and giving thee moreover a swan-drawn chariot to drive, would have thee go to Delphi and the water which is Cephissus' gift to Castaly, there to deliver justice and right in oracles unto Greece; nevertheless, once mounted, thou badest thy swans fly to the land of the Hyperboreans; and although when the Delphians heard of it they set a paean unto flutes and dances of youths around the tripod and besought thee to come

e. g. thence, yet for a whole year dealtest thou law in that country; then when it was time for the tripods of Delphi, too, to give sound, thou badest the swans fly back thither. Now it was summer and the midst of summer when thou returnedst from the Hyperboreans; the nightingale sang and the swallow, the cricket sang also to tell mankind of thy fortunes, while Castaly flowed with springs of silver, and great Cephissus lifted his shining waves well knowing that a God was come home.

poems.title: To Hermes (Fragment 2)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book I, Hymns
poems.text: Hail, thou ruler of Cyllene! thee it is my will to sing, whom Maia bare upon the breezy heights unto the love of the omnipotent Son of Cronus.

poems.title: Fragment 4
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book I, Hymns
poems.text: e.g. And when thou stolest away the oxen of Apollo, 'tis true he found them, being Lord of divination; but when he threatened thee full direly, then thou stolest away the very bow and arrows that were upon his shoulder: whereat he smiled, and gave thee the divining-staff from which men know thee to this day as 'God of the golden wand,' and himself received from thee the lyre whence he is called 'Wielder of gold.'

poems.title: To Athena (Fragment 6)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book I, Hymns
poems.text: O Queen Athena, upholder of War, who standest, we know, watching over Coronea before a stream-flanked temple on the banks of the Coalius . . .

poems.title: To Ares (Fragment 10)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book I, Hymns
poems.text: O War, through whom murderous Fear . . .

poems.title: Fragment 12
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book I, Hymns
poems.text: . . . and may thy daughter lead the enterprise!

poems.title: To Love (Fragment 13)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book I, Hymns
poems.text: . . . awfullest of Gods, whom sandalled Iris bore to Zephyr of the golden hair

poems.title: To the Dioscuri (Fragment 14)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book I, Hymns
poems.text: Come ye hither from star-bright Olympus, ye stalwart children of Zeus and Leda, and shine forth in propitious wise, O Castor and Polydeuces, who go on swift-footed horses over broad earth and all the sea, and do so easily save men from lamentable death by leaping to the high-top of benched barks, there to sit far-seen upon the forestays, and so lighting to the midnight path of the black ship . . .

poems.title: To Achilles (Fragment 15)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book I, Hymns
poems.text: O King Achilles, who rulest the land of Scythia . . .

poems.title: Fragment 16
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book I, Hymns
poems.text: O Nymphs, who they say are sprung from the Aegis-Bearer . . .

poems.title: To the Sun (Fragment 17)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book I, Hymns
poems.text: Allnurturing Sun, who hast come by river-banks or by the purple sea where the gushing wave beats on the surfy shore, while many maids stand in a ring and rub with dainty hands the flesh of their fair thighs, taking and pouring the gentle water over themselves even as an unguent . . .

poems.title: To Poverty (Fragment 18)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book I, Hymns
poems.text: O Poverty, thou grievous and resistless ill, who with thy sister Helplessness overwhelmest a great people . . .

poems.title: Fragment 19
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book II, War-Songs
poems.text: The great house is all agleam with bronze. War has bedecked the whole roof with bright helmets, from which hang waving horse-hair plumes to make adornment for the heads of men; the pegs are hidden with bright brazen greaves to ward off the strong arrow, corslets of new linen cloth and hollow shields are piled upon the floor, and beside them stand swords of Chalcidian steel, and many a doublet, many a kilt. These we cannot forget, so soon as ever we undertake this task.

poems.title: Fragment 20
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book II, War-Songs
poems.text: and tossing a Carian plume

poems.title: Fragment 21
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book II, War-Songs
poems.text: They cowered like birds at the sudden sight of a swift eagle.

poems.title: Fragment 22
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book II, War-Songs
poems.text: greater warriors than the War-God

poems.title: Fragment 23
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book II, War-Songs
poems.text: for 'tis noble to die in war;

poems.title: Fragment 24
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book II, War-Songs
poems.text: They mingled war one against another.

poems.title: Fragment 25
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book II, War-Songs
poems.text: Verily she did join together a divided host of men by inspiring it with law and order.

poems.title: Fragment 26
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book II, War-Songs
poems.text: . . . as for me, when grievous age wears me out, then be it not mine to forget the kindness of such as were my friends of old.

poems.title: To Mytilene (Fragment 27)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book II, War-Songs
poems.text: Now is our song of thee, thou great Nurse of all those tender youths who recking so little of themselves took the field in the first rank of our people; for they have done the allotted task of men with the same will as those who have grown to be men. Were I all-wise, were I like to a God in shrewdness of wit, even so I would not so much as pluck out a hair contrary to the decree of Zeus, and being grown men our lives are mingled with troubles befitting our estate; but for youths to rush into the deep tumult of the battle mellay—that is not for them. [Yet these, when a host ill-conquerable came up against our city, laid fear aside and took arms and . . . .]

poems.title: Fragment 28
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book II, War-Songs
poems.text: Not houses finely roofed or the stones of walls well-builded, nay nor canals and dockyards, make the city, but men able to use their opportunity.

poems.title: Fragment 29
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book II, War-Songs
poems.text: Not stone and timber, nor the craft of the joiner, make the city; but wheresoever are men who know how to keep themselves safe, there are walls and there a city.

poems.title: Fragment 30
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book II, War-Songs
poems.text: For blazons wound not nor of themselves carry pain, except he that wields them, if he be a noble man.

poems.title: Fragment 31
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book II, War-Songs
poems.text: to whom you shall be an unbridleable defence.

poems.title: Fragment 32
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book II, War-Songs
poems.text: . . . when thou savest them from destruction.

poems.title: Fragment 33
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book II, War-Songs
poems.text: . . . and to sail thither in ships

poems.title: Fragment 36
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: . . . between earth and snowy sky;

poems.title: Fragment 37
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: I cannot tell the lie of the wind; one wave rolls from this quarter, another from that, and we are carried in the midst with the black ship, labouring in an exceeding great storm. The water is up to the mast-hole, and the sail lets daylight through with the great rents that are in it, and the halyards are working loose.

poems.title: Fragment 38
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: Lo now! the wave that is to windward of us comes this way, and will give us sore labour to bale it out when it breaks over us.

poems.title: Fragment 40
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: nor had Poseidon yet roughened the salt sea

poems.title: To his Country (Fragment 41)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: What purpose or intent is in thee, O Country, that thou hast been so long time distraught? Be of good cheer; for the son of Cronus himself did tell thee that thou hadst no need to fear warfare howsoever it should seize thee, nor should neighbour foeman, nay nor oarsman from over the far-bounded sea, maintain for long the woeful conflict of the far-flung spear, unless thou shouldst of thyself send afar all the best of thy people, to sunder them from thee. For 'tis men that are a city's tower in war. But alas! thou no longer doest the Father's will, and so a swift fate hath overtaken thee, and us that had been sent to help thee, Zeus—for so he had willed it—hath made to miscarry and taken away from thee again. And let whoso will bring thee assuagement of thy woes. He that hath made him pottage, he also must eat it; these things are no longer a concern of ours. And whatsoever Fate it is that sendeth this trouble, 'tis sent with good reason. These woes began for thee with Tenages, son of Aeolus, that was slain of yore by the sword of his brother Macar, a sword that left sorrow behind it. And now I make this prayer concerning thee: that I may no longer see the daylight, if the son of Cleanax or yonder Splitfoot or the son of Archeanax be suffered yet to live by one whom his dear sweet native-land, and factious strife as old as itself, together have done away.

poems.title: Fragment 42
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: 'Tis time for wine and time for women, now that Myrsilus is dead.

poems.title: Fragment 43
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: and if Zeus will accomplish what is our intent;

poems.title: Fragment 44
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: the immortal Gods have given us the victory;

poems.title: Fragment 45
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: He struck him mad altogether and took his wits away.

poems.title: Fragment 47
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: Melanchros, being worthy of his country's respect

poems.title: Fragment 48
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: e.g. For when I was fighting the Erythraeans, Apollo came unto me in my sleep with a tamarisk branch in his hand.

poems.title: Fragment 49
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: For the prerogative which belongs to you by grace of the Gods, he will make the prerogative of insatiate men.

poems.title: Fragment 50
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: This man with his longing for great power will quickly overturn his country; she is tottering now;

poems.title: To Pittacus (Fragment 53)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: O thou destroyer of hips and haws—for 'tis no shame to an Arcadian [to be called that] . . .

poems.title: Fragment 54
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: The Arcadians were eaters of acorns.

poems.title: Fragment 55
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: Near to your house and near to your infamies . . .

poems.title: Fragment 56
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: And now this fellow has prevailed, by moving the piece on the sacred line, the cunning man.

poems.title: Fragment 57
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: Over Tantalus' head, O son of Aesimus, there hung a great stone;

poems.title: Fragment 58
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: And are the weapons still lying bright and ready in the myrtle-grove for Dinnomenes and the son of Hyrrhas?

poems.title: To Pittacus (Fragment 59)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: . . . and you drain goblets sitting beside Dinnomenes,

poems.title: Fragment 62
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: He's stirring up the pigs again;

poems.title: Fragment 66
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: painting a lion from the claw,

poems.title: Fragment 67
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: e.g. 'Tis said that wrath is the last thing in a man to grow old.

poems.title: To Zeus (Fragment 68)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: . . . he doth not take up. Make thou far-darting, Father, and unerring the heart of yonder man, Father, but all such as are inspired by the shameless one make thou a sinful thing of hate.

poems.title: To Zeus (Fragment 69)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: Father Zeus, though the Lydians, in other men's time of misfortune and having received no benefit at our hands and knowing us not at all, gave us two thousand staters in the hope we might reach the sacred city, this fellow like a cunning-hearted fox made fair promises [to his own fellow-citizens] and then reckoned he would escape scotfree [if he failed to perform them].

poems.title: Fragment 70
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: . . . to say to him: 'He who shared evil revels with an unseemly crew, as a mere stone of the base, now, by making merry with good-fellows of the idlest and vainest, has become the headstone over them all.' And in the pride of his marriage with a daughter of Atreus let him do despite to his countrymen as he did with Myrsilus, till Ares choose to turn our luck and we forget this our anger and have rest from the heart-devouring pain and internecine battle which one of the Olympians hath roused in us to bring destruction on the people and to give delightful glory unto Pittacus.

poems.title: Fragment 71
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: You were friends enough with me once to be invited to sup on kid and pork; this is the way of the world.

poems.title: To Pittacus (Fragment 72)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: . . . and garnering his plunderous crop, fills the whole house both day and night with unmixed wine, and wassailings have been brought in unto the place where the law is wont to speak; and yon man forgot them not, so soon as he had overthrown him; for he set them a-going every night, and the bottom of the flagon rang and rang again. Aye, you that come of such lineage have the honour and glory enjoyed by the free sons of noble parents . . .

poems.title: Fragment 73
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: . . . The sailors have cast all their cargo overboard and are saving themselves as best they can. Meanwhile, beaten with the roaring wave, the ship bethinks her that she no longer desires to fight with storm and tempest but would willingly strike a reef and go to the bottom. That is her plight; but as for me, dear comrades, I would forget these things and make merry here both with you and with Bacchus! And yet why take we our love off our country, even though fools have thrown all she hath into confusion, mingling . . .

poems.title: To Mytilene (Fragment 74)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: . . . Nor yet did he harm thee in that he itched, as every child of unfamed parents itches, to go in and out of garish houses; for being still at home among the obscure, he was bearable as yet. But when he did the deeds of wicked men in wanton presumption and drunken with power, there was no bearing such things as those. And now after many a slip we stand upright in our ancient estate; [for though these sweets] are mingled with that [sour], still God, I ween, [decrees us something bad in everything that is good.]

poems.title: Fragment 75
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: . . . and as for me, I remember it not; for I was still a little child sitting on his nurse's knee; but I know from my father the honour yon man had received of yore from the son of Penthilus; and 'now he that overturned the despotism of the traitor [Melanchros, is himself, ere we knew it], become despot [of our city].'

poems.title: To the Mytileneans (Fragment 76)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: . . . But he goes striding wide over your heads, and you hold your tongues like initiates when they behold the dead they have called up. Nay rather, my fellow-countrymen, up and quench the log while it but smoulders among you, lest the light thereof come to a brighter flame.

poems.title: Fragment 77
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: You were not altogether a knave . . . , . . . , nor yet a fool, but kept the oath you swore to us by the altar of the Son of Leto, that none of the Children of Treason should know truly who it was to whom in the beginning . . .

poems.title: Fragment 78
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: . . . nor make troubles for those who are more than we.

poems.title: Fragment 79
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books III-IV, Political Songs
poems.text: . . . whoever of you and us are good men.

poems.title: Fragment 81
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VI, Unclassifiable Fragments
poems.text: . . . For even as once on a day 'tis told Aristodemus said at Sparta—and 'twas no bad thing—, the money is the man, and no poor man is either good or honourable.

poems.title: Fragment 82
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VI, Unclassifiable Fragments
poems.text: . . . And to drink seemed to him a pleasant thing; but one that hath so much wine as that about his wits, such an one lives no life at all; for he hangs his head, chiding oft his own heart and repenting him of what he hath done. And so it ceased to please him when he came to his ripest.

poems.title: Fragment 83
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VI, Unclassifiable Fragments
poems.text: Sprung from the royal son of Cronus, Ajax second in valour to Achilles . . .

poems.title: Fragment 84
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VI, Unclassifiable Fragments
poems.text: For he is the shaker of the earth;

poems.title: Fragment 85
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VI, Unclassifiable Fragments
poems.text: Child of the rock and the grey sea . . . and thou fillest all hearts with pride, thou lepas of the sea.

poems.title: Fragment 86
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VI, Unclassifiable Fragments
poems.text: Me a woman miserable, me a sharer in all misfortune

poems.title: Fragment 87
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VI, Unclassifiable Fragments
poems.text: and ruled over full many peoples.

poems.title: Fragment 90
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VI, Unclassifiable Fragments
poems.text: These things began, 'tis said, with our fathers.

poems.title: Fragment 92
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VI, Unclassifiable Fragments
poems.text: and a fearful madness springs up in the breast of the hart;

poems.title: Fragment 93
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VI, Unclassifiable Fragments
poems.text: e.g. . . . O Hebrus, fairest of all rivers

poems.title: Fragment 96
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VI, Unclassifiable Fragments
poems.text: e.g. . . . The Phaeacians, sprung from drops celestial

poems.title: Fragment 112
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VI, Unclassifiable Fragments
poems.text: but when they swam with their hands . . . ;

poems.title: Fragment 120
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VI, Unclassifiable Fragments
poems.text: . . . Through Helen 'tis said there sprang from evil deeds a branch bitter unto Priam and all the Trojans, and a flame rolled around sacred Ilium. Not such was the dainty maiden whom the son of Aeacus, with all the Gods gathered at his longed-for spousals, took from the palace of Nereus and led home to the house of Cheiron, where the love that was betwixt the noble Peleus and the best of all the Nereids loosed the girdle of a pure virgin, and bore them a year afterwards a son that was mightiest of demigods, a victorious driver of bay steeds; but the Trojans and their city were destroyed because of Helen.

poems.title: To Melanippus (Fragment 121)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VII, Love-Poems
poems.text: [Speed thee, herald, to lovely Mytilene and say to my dearest Melanippus:] 'Your Alcaeus is safe as you see, but not his arms; that shield of everlasting might the Athenians have hung up in the temple of the Grey-Eyed Goddess.'

poems.title: To Melanippus (Fragment 122)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VII, Love-Poems
poems.text: O why, Melanippus, do you pray you might be with me? or why, when once Fate has sent me to eddying Acheron, shall I hope to re-cross it and see again the pure light of the sun? Nay, set not your desire on things too great. King Sisyphus son of Aeolus, he thought with a craft unsurpassed to have escaped death; but for all his cunning he crossed the eddying Acheron in fate the second time, and the Son of Cronus ordained that he should have below a toil the woefullest in all the world. So I pray you bewail not these things. If ever cries were unavailing, our cries are unavailing now. Assuredly some of these things were to be suffered with an enduring heart. When the wind rises in the north [no skilful pilot puts out into the wide sea.]

poems.title: To Menon (Fragment 123)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VII, Love-Poems
poems.text: I bid them call the pretty Menon, if I may have him for an added joy at my drinking-bout.

poems.title: Fragment 124
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VII, Love-Poems
poems.text: Pure Sappho of the violet tresses and the gentle smile, I would fain tell you something, did not shame prevent me.

poems.title: Fragment 125
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VII, Love-Poems
poems.text: Pray, pray receive, receive your serenader.

poems.title: Fragment 126
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VII, Love-Poems
poems.text: Wine, my dear boy, and truth . . .

poems.title: Fragment 127
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VII, Love-Poems
poems.text: . . . for I do not reckon Lycus among the Muses;

poems.title: Fragment 128
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VII, Love-Poems
poems.text: I am thrown by the wily arts of the Cyprus-born; for whithersoever [on sea or land I flee, thither] ranging [hath Love overtaken me.]

poems.title: Fragment 129
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VII, Love-Poems
poems.text: the soft smooth bloom of the fruiting-time

poems.title: Fragment 132
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VII, Love-Poems
poems.text: You have made me forget all my sorrows

poems.title: To Antimenidas (Fragment 133)
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VIII, Encomia
poems.text: You have come from the ends of the earth, [dear Antimenidas,] with the gold-bound ivory heft of the sword [with which, fighting for the Babylonians who dwell in houses of bricks four hands long, you performed a mighty deed and saved them all from grievous troubles] by slaying a warrior who wanted but one palm's breadth of five royal cubits of stature.

poems.title: Fragment 134
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VIII, Encomia
poems.text: . . . of sacred Babylon . . . Ascalon . . .

poems.title: Fragment 138
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VIII, Encomia
poems.text: Deeply do I mourn, for my friends are nothing worth.

poems.title: Fragment 139
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VIII, Encomia
poems.text: If you say what you choose, you will hear what you choose not.

poems.title: Fragment 141
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VIII, Encomia
poems.text: What birds are these which have come from the ends of the earth and the ocean, wildgeese of motley neck and widespread wing?

poems.title: Fragment 142
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VIII, Encomia
poems.text: For even if he comes from another place, he can always say that he is come from that.

poems.title: Fragment 143
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VIII, Encomia
poems.text: If you move from a stone-heap a block of stone that is not firm set, then 'tis like you will get a sore head.

poems.title: Fragment 144
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VIII, Encomia
poems.text: . . . nor prevaricating his intent at all;

poems.title: Fragment 145
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VIII, Encomia
poems.text: For my part I find no witnesses of this;

poems.title: Fragment 146
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VIII, Encomia
poems.text: We learn from our fathers

poems.title: Fragment 151
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VIII, Encomia
poems.text: . . . takes bites of the cucumbers;

poems.title: Fragment 154
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VIII, Encomia
poems.text: Asking for a pig in place of a bad dog;

poems.title: Fragment 155
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Book VIII, Encomia
poems.text: In fleeing the ashes he's fallen into the coals;

poems.title: Fragment 157
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: The Sky-God bows himself; there is a great storm in the heavens, the streams of water are frozen fast. . . . Defy the storm with a good fire and a bountiful mixing of honey-sweet wine, and then put a soft cushion on either side your brow.

poems.title: Fragment 158
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: It is ill yielding the heart to mischance; for we shall make no advance if we weary of thee, O Bacchus, and the best medicine is to call for wine and drink deep.

poems.title: Fragment 159
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: But let them put garlands woven of anise about our necks and pour sweet myrrh over our bosoms.

poems.title: Fragment 160
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: With one voice they have set up the base-born Pittacus to be tyrant of their spiritless and ill-starred country, shouting his praise by their thousands.

poems.title: Fragment 161
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: Soak your throttle in wine; for the star is coming round again, the season is hard to bear with the world athirst because of the heat; the cricket sounds sweetly from the leaves of the tree-top, and lo! the artichoke is blowing; now are women at their sauciest, but men lean and weak because Sirius parches both the head and the knees.

poems.title: Fragment 162
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: Let us drink, for the star is coming round.

poems.title: Fragment 163
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: Let us drink; why wait for the lamp-lighting? the day has but a finger's breadth to go. Take down the great cups, beloved friend, from the cupboard; for the Son of Semele and Zeus gave wine to make us forget our cares. Pour bumpers in a mixture of one and two; and let cup chase cup around hotfoot;

poems.title: Fragment 164
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: Over my long-suffering head, over my hoary breast, pour me the unguent. If any man be in pain, then let him drink. [To all men soon or late the Olympians] give misfortune, [and this woe of mine I share] with other men. And as for him that [says there is] no [good in drinking], you may say to him 'Be hanged with you! [you know not good from bad.']

poems.title: Fragment 165
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: . . . the stormless breath of light winds

poems.title: Fragment 166
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text:
I heard the flowery Spring beginning;

make haste and mix a bowl of the honey-sweet.

poems.title: Fragment 167
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: Plant no tree sooner than the vine.

poems.title: Fragment 168
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: drawing it sometimes honey-sweet, and sometimes as bitter as burdocks

poems.title: Fragment 169
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: for wine is a spying-hole unto man.

poems.title: Fragment 170
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: Hail, and drink this!

poems.title: Fragment 171
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: Hither, and drink with me.

poems.title: Fragment 172
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: The heeltaps fly from Teian cups;

poems.title: Fragment 173
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: and nothing will come of anything;

poems.title: Fragment 175
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. I (Loeb, 1922): Books IX-X, Drinking-Songs
poems.text: for woeful decrepitude is coming.

poems.title: Fragment 1: Χαῖρε, Κυλλάνας ὁ μέδεις
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Χαῖρε, Κυλλάνας ὁ μέδεις, σὲ γάρ μοι
θῦμος ὕμνην, τὸν κορύφαισ᾽ ἐν ἄγναις
Μαῖα γέννατο Κρονίδα μίγεισα
παμβασίληϊ.

poems.title: Fragment 2: Ϝάνασσ᾽ Ἀθανάα πολεμάδοκος
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Ϝάνασσ᾽ Ἀθανάα πολεμάδοκος,
ἅ ποι Κορωνείας ἐπιδεύαο
ναύω πάροιθεν ἀμφὶ ⟨βώμῳ⟩,
Κωραλίω ποτάμω παρ᾽ ὄχθαις.

poems.title: Fragment 3: δεινότατον θέων
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
δεινότατον θέων
⟨τὸν⟩ γέννατ᾽ εὐπέδιλλος Ἶρις
χρυσοκόμᾳ Ζεφύρῳ μίγεισα.

poems.title: Fragment 4: Ἀσυνέτημι τῶν ἀνέμων στάσιν
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Ἀσυνέτημι τῶν ἀνέμων στάσιν·
τὸ μὲν γὰρ ἔνθεν κῦμα κυλίνδεται,
τὸ δ᾽ ἔνθεν· ἄμμες δ᾽ ὖν τὸ μέσσον
νᾶϊ φορήμεθα σὺν μελαίνᾳ,
χείμωνι μοχθεῦντες μεγάλῳ μάλα·
πὲρ μὲν γὰρ ἄντλος ἰστοπέδαν ἔχει,
λαῖφος δὲ πὰν ζάδηλον ἤδη
καὶ λάκιδες μεγάλαι κατ᾽ αὖτο·
χόλαισι δ᾽ ἄγκυλαι.

poems.title: Fragment 5: Τὸ δ᾽ αὖτε κῦμα
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Τὸ δ᾽ αὖτε κῦμα τῶν προτέρων ὄνω
στείχει, παρέξει δ᾽ ἄμμι πόνον πόλυν
ἄντλην, ἐπεί κε νᾶος ἔμβᾳ

poems.title: Fragment 6: Νῦν χρῆ μεθύσθην καί
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Νῦν χρῆ μεθύσθην καί τινα πρὸς βίαν
πώνην, ἐπειδὴ κάτθανε Μύρσιλος.

poems.title: Fragment 7: τὸ γὰρ Ἄρευϊ κατθάνην κάλον
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
τὸ γὰρ
Ἄρευϊ κατθάνην κάλον.

poems.title: Fragment 8: Ἔπταξον ὥστ᾽ ὄρνιθες ὠκὺν
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Ἔπταξον ὥστ᾽ ὄρνιθες ὠκὺν
αἴετον ἐξαπίνας φάνεντα.

poems.title: Fragment 9: Ὕει μὲν ὁ Ζεῦς
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Ὕει μὲν ὁ Ζεῦς, ἐκ δ᾽ ὀράνω μέγας
χειμών, πεπάγασιν δ᾽ ὑδάτων ῥόαι,

κάββαλλε τὸν χείμων᾽, ἐπὶ μὲν τίθεις
πῦρ, ἐν δὲ κέρναις οἶνον ἀφειδέως
μέλιχρον, αὐτὰρ ἀμφὶ κόρσᾳ
μάλθακον ἀμφὶ ⟨βάλων⟩ γνόφαλλον.

poems.title: Fragment 10: Οὐ χρῆ κάκοισι θῦμον
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Οὐ χρῆ κάκοισι θῦμον ἐπιτρέπην·
προκόψομεν γὰρ οὐδὲν ἀσάμενοι,
ὦ Βύκχι, φάρμακον δ᾽ ἄριστον
οἶνον ἐνεικαμένοις μεθύσθην.

poems.title: Fragment 11: Οἶνος γὰρ ἀνθρώποισι δίοπτρον
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text: Οἶνος γὰρ ἀνθρώποισι δίοπτρον.

poems.title: Fragment 12: Θέλω τι Ϝείπην, ἀλλά
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Θέλω τι Ϝείπην, ἀλλά με κωλύει
αἴδως.

poems.title: Fragment 13: Ἰόπλοκ᾽ ἄγνα μελλιχόμειδε Σάπφοι
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text: Ἰόπλοκ᾽ ἄγνα μελλιχόμειδε Σάπφοι

poems.title: Fragment 14: Ἀλλ᾽ ἀνήτω μὲν περὶ
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Ἀλλ᾽ ἀνήτω μὲν περὶ ταῖς δέραισι
περθέτω πλέκταις ὑποθύμιδάς τις,
κὰδ δὲ χευάτω μύρον ἆδυ κὰτ τῶ
στήθεος ἄμμι.

poems.title: Fragment 15: Ἄνδρες γὰρ πόλιος πύργος
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text: Ἄνδρες γὰρ πόλιος πύργος ἀρεύιοι.

poems.title: Fragment 16: Ἦλθες ἐκ περάτων γᾶς
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Ἦλθες ἐκ περάτων γᾶς ἐλεφαντίναν
λάβαν τῶ ξίφεος χρυσοδέταν ἔχων,
⟨ἐπειδὴ⟩ μέγαν ἄθλον Βαβυλωνίοις
συμμάχεις τέλεσας, ῥύσαο δ᾽ ἐκ πόνων,
κτένναις ἄνδρα μαχαίταν βασιληΐων
παλαίσταν ἀπυλείποντα μόναν ἴαν
παχέων ἀπὺ πέμπων.

poems.title: Fragment 17: νῦν δ᾽ οὗτος ἐπικρέτει
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
νῦν δ᾽ οὗτος ἐπικρέτει
κιννήσαις τὸν ἀπ᾽ ἰρᾶς πυκινῶς λίθον.

poems.title: Fragment 18: τὸν κακοπάτριδα Πίττακον
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
τὸν κακοπάτριδα
Πίττακον πόλιος τᾶς ἀχόλω καὶ βαρυδαίμονος
ἐστάσαντο τύραννον μέγ᾽ ἐπαίνεντες ἀόλλεες.

poems.title: Fragment 19: Τέγγε πλεύμονα Ϝοίνῳ· τὸ
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Τέγγε πλεύμονα Ϝοίνῳ· τὸ γὰρ ἄστρον περιτέλλεται,
ἁ δ᾽ ὥρα χαλέπα, πάντα δὲ δίψαισ᾽ ὑπὰ καύματος,
ἄχει δ᾽ ἐκ πετάλων Ϝάδεα τέττιξ, πτερύγων δ᾽ ὔπο
κακχέει λιγύραν ⟨πύκνον⟩ ἀοίδαν, ⟨σέλας⟩ ὄπποτα
φλόγιον κατὰ γᾶν πεπτάμενον ⟨πάντα⟩ καταυάνῃ·
ἄνθει καὶ σκόλυμος· νῦν δὲ γύναικες μιαρώταται,
λέπτοι δ᾽ ἄνδρες, ἐπεὶ ⟨καὶ⟩ κεφάλαν καὶ γόνα Σείριος
ἄζει.

poems.title: Fragment 20: Πίνωμεν· τί τὰ λύχν᾽
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Πίνωμεν· τί τὰ λύχν᾽ ὀμμένομεν; δάκτυλος ἀμέρα.
κὰδ δ᾽ ἄερρε κυλίχναις μεγάλαις, αὔιτα, ποικίλαις·
οἶνον γὰρ Σεμέλας καὶ Δίος υἷος λαθικάδεα
ἀνθρώποισιν ἔδωκ᾽· ἔγχεε κέρναις ἔνα καὶ δύο
πλέαις κὰκ κεφάλας· ἁ δ᾽ ἀτέρα τὰν ἀτέραν κύλιξ
ὠθήτω.

poems.title: Fragment 21: Κὰτ τᾶς πόλλα παθοίσας
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Κὰτ τᾶς πόλλα παθοίσας κεφάλας κακχεάτω μύρον
καὶ κὰτ τῶ πολίω στήθεος.

poems.title: Fragment 22: Μηδὲν ἄλλο φυτεύσῃς πρότερον
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text: Μηδὲν ἄλλο φυτεύσῃς πρότερον δένδριον ἀμπέλω.

poems.title: Fragment 23: Αἴ κ᾽ εἴπῃς τὰ
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Αἴ κ᾽ εἴπῃς τὰ θέλεις, ⟨αὐτὸς⟩ ἀκούσαις ⟨κε⟩ τά κ᾽ οὐ
[θέλοις].

poems.title: Fragment 24: Μαρμαίρει δὲ μέγας δόμος
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Μαρμαίρει δὲ μέγας δόμος χάλκῳ· πᾶσα δ᾽ Ἄρῃ κεκόσμηται στέγα
λάμπραισιν κυνίαισι, κὰτ τῶν λεῦκοι κατύπερθεν ἵππιοι λόφοι
νεύοισιν, κεφάλαισιν ἄνδρων ἀγάλματα· χάλκιαι δὲ πασσάλοις
κρύπτοισιν περικείμεναι λάμπραι κνάμιδες, ἄρκος ἰσχύρω βέλευς,
θώρακές τε νέω λίνω κούιλαί τε κὰτ ἄσπιδες βεβλήμεναι·
πὰρ δὲ Χαλκίδικαι σπάθαι, πὰρ δὲ ζώμματα πόλλα καὶ κυπάσσιδες·
τῶν οὐκ ἔστι λάθεσθ᾽, ἐπειδὴ πρώτιστ᾽ ὑπὰ Ϝέργον
ἔσταμεν τόδε.

poems.title: Fragment 25: Ὥς γὰρ δή ποτ᾽
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Ὥς γὰρ δή ποτ᾽ Ἀριστόδαμον φᾶσ᾽ οὐκ ἀπάλαμνον ἐν Σπάρτᾳ λόγον
εἴπην· “χρήματ᾽ ἄνηρ”· πένιχρος δ᾽ οὔδεις πέλετ᾽ ἔσλος
οὐδὲ τίμιος.

poems.title: Fragment 26: Κρονίδα βασίληος γένος Αἶαν
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text: Κρονίδα βασίληος γένος Αἶαν, τὸν ἄριστον πεδ᾽ Ἀχίλλεα.

poems.title: Fragment 27: Κόλπῳ σ᾽ ἐδέξαντ᾽ ἄγναι
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text: Κόλπῳ σ᾽ ἐδέξαντ᾽ ἄγναι Χάριτες, Κρόκοι.

poems.title: Fragment 28: Ἦρος ἀνθεμόεντος ἐπάιον ἐρχομένοιο
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Ἦρος ἀνθεμόεντος ἐπάιον ἐρχομένοιο·
ἐν δὲ κέρνατε τῶ μελιάδεος ὄττι τάχιστα
κράτηρα.

poems.title: Fragment 29: Ἀργάλιον πενία κάκον ἄσχετον
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Ἀργάλιον πενία κάκον ἄσχετον, ἃ μέγα δάμναι
λᾶον ἀμαχανίᾳ σὺν ἀδελφίᾳ.

poems.title: Fragment 30: Ὤνηρ οὗτος ὁ μαιόμενος
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text:
Ὤνηρ οὗτος ὁ μαιόμενος τὸ μέγα κρέτος
ὀντρέψει τάχα τὰν πόλιν· ἁ δ᾽ ἔχεται ῥόπας.

poems.title: Fragment 31: Κεῖσθαι πὲρ κεφάλας μέγας
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text: Κεῖσθαι πὲρ κεφάλας μέγας, ὦ Αἰσιμίδα, λίθος

poems.title: Fragment 32: Οἶνος, ὦ φίλε παῖ
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text: Οἶνος, ὦ φίλε παῖ, καὶ ἀλάθεα.

poems.title: Fragment 33: Ἔμε δείλαν, ἔμε παῖσαν
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text: Ἔμε δείλαν, ἔμε παῖσαν κακοτάτων πεδέχοισαν.

poems.title: Fragment 34: Δέξαι με κωμάζοντα, δέξαι
poems.author: Alcaeus of Lesbos
poems.collection: Greek Melic Poets (Smyth, 1900): Alcaeus, Greek text
poems.text: Δέξαι με κωμάζοντα, δέξαι, λίσσομαι σε, λίσσομαι.
